newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-COOK WINS BOB HOPE CLASSIC WITH RECORD SCORE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-COOK WINS BOB HOPE CLASSIC WITH RECORD SCORE.

text.p: John Cook won the Bob Hope Chrysler Classic in record fashion, shooting weekend rounds of 62-63 at Indian Wells to beat a fading Mark Calcavecchia by a stroke on Sunday.

Cook was nine under par over the last 18 holes to finish at 33 under par for the five-round event played over four courses. One shot back at 328 was Calcavecchia, who shot 67 and let a four-stroke lead slip away in the final round.
Said Cook, who played his last 36 holes at the Indian Wells course, "I made 20 birdies in the last two days. Wow! I hope I didn't use up my quota for the year."
Cook collected $270,000 for the victory, the ninth of his career and second in the Hope, which he also won in 1992.

Cook's Saturday and Sunday total of 125 matched the PGA Tour record for consecutive rounds. That score has been shot five times now, the last man to do it was Cook himself, who shot 62-63 when he won in Memphis last July.
Cook's 327 total is the second best for a 90-hole event -- Tom Kite won here in 1993 with a score of 35 under par.
"When I get on a golf course like this one that plays into my hands like this one does, I feel like I'm in control of my game, and I'm comfortable with every club in the bag," said Cook.

Calcavecchia had started the final round with a three-shot lead over Cook, and only two other golfers within nine strokes. After four holes his lead had increased to four strokes, but Cook drew level on the 11th hole.

The tie was broken on the 17th, as Calcavecchia's drive clipped a eucalyptus tree branch and dropped down some 65 yards from the tee. He had to lay up on the par four and made his only bogey of the day, allowing Cook to play the final hole with a one-shot lead.

Said Calcavecchia, "I hit a bad shot, but I'm human. Where I feel I lost the tournament was missing some short putts on the front nine. There were a few holes there where my putter felt like a spatula."

For Cook, who now tops the PGA Tour money list with $305,600, this was his third victory since July. It marks his emergence from a pronounced slump, a revival sparked by a two-day session with his mentor, Ken Venturi, last March.
"I was tired of being a regular guy, looking at the board on Friday to see if I made the cut," said Cook. "That's not me. I'm out here to do better than that. It seems like I'm on my way now."
